whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls Back

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but claims against a government entity — like a city road agency — can require notice in as little as six months. An attorney can help make sure deadlines aren't missed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Both Ways
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present evidence that fairly reflects how the crash actually happened.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California doesn't cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases. Working with an attorney on contingency means there's no upfront cost to find out what your claim may be worth.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use recorded statements to look for reasons to reduce or deny a claim. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: I was in a crash near Aliso Viejo Parkway — does the time of day matter?
items.answer: Reported crashes in Aliso Viejo tend to cluster on Fridays in the afternoon, which can mean more witnesses and traffic camera footage available near intersections like Aliso Viejo Parkway. An attorney can help gather that evidence quickly before it's lost or overwritten.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after you're matched.
